pillar_reactions.evidence: Understood and agreed with no questions — 'No. I assume. And it was this, like, I'm not dumb to fitness or working out or other things, and so, no, this is exactly what I anticipated.' He engaged most with the functional-strength framing, which matched language he had used himself earlier: 'I don't really need the impact of running miles and miles, or squatting real, real heavy stuff. I need functional strength is what it is.' He also supplied his own proof point — 'These are kettlebells in real life' — connecting the rotational demands of golf to the training. The pillar had very little to establish because the prospect had pre-sold himself on the modality from YouTube months earlier.

Clean acceptance and mostly validation of what he already does — 'No, no, I'm comfortable with, you know, I could certainly clean it up a bit, but again, we eat very well as it is.' Baseline had already established a half-cow of beef in the freezer, local farm produce, high protein, deliberate avoidance of sprayed food, and a self-taught intermittent fast on a six-to-eight-hour window. The one useful disclosure came through this pillar: he tends to become rigid and all-or-nothing about protocols — 'if you have a half teaspoon of sugar, you've ruined your fast... The day is completely ruined if I add anything to it. I'll kind of get obsessive about it' — and the rep correctly pushed back on that.

Volunteered the strongest reaction of the call, before the rep had finished — 'Okay. This is the big one' and 'the accountability part's huge.' He mapped it straight onto his own history: 'powerlifting as a, when I was in high school, there was a coach, you had to show up for practices with wrestling, man, go run and then go train for two hours.' And he named the mechanism that would work on him: 'you don't want to let him down too... I don't want to let my team down at work, the corporate down. I don't want to let Trevor down if we do this.' He had also raised the weekly check-in unprompted much earlier in the call. This is the pillar that sold him.

anchors.raw: I bought $1,000 worth of equipment two years ago to set in my garage, right, and just sat there, and my wife was like, you're not going to use it, you know, and even that, like her even doubting whether I'm going to use it or not, I don't need a bunch of equipment, I need a kettlebell or two, and I'll prove everybody wrong
anchors.competitor: His own unused home gym equipment
anchors.note: Works in both directions and is the most interesting anchor on the call. As evidence it undercuts — a documented $1,000 failure to follow through, witnessed and predicted by the person who now controls the budget, which is exactly the argument his wife can make in three weeks. As motivation it supports, because he has turned it into a chip on his shoulder. The rep noticed neither use and never brought it back when the spouse conversation arrived.

anchors.raw: I'm sure you listen to Joe Rogan, he talks about his, all he works out with are kettlebells, right? And it's the same thing, and it's like, that guy's physique is crazy.
anchors.note: The prospect supplied his own third-party validation for the modality, unprompted, before any pitch. Consistent with the pattern across this batch that the modality is pre-sold by media and the call is only selling coaching around it.

anchors.raw: we're about to put kids in school, and we're going to do some private school. So I didn't realize it was 6,000, but I do need to, we're going to re-budget, or like basically change our budget status based on private school
anchors.competitor: Private school fees for three boys
anchors.note: The real competitor is not another fitness product but a school bill landing in the same month as the family relocation. Combined with 'I didn't realize it was 6,000', this is a price that arrived unframed into a tightening budget — which is what P1's four-part frame is supposed to prevent.

anchors.raw: I've got a huge job. I'll probably make like a $50,000 profit on it that's going to come into my finances. So when I can do that, I would comfortably be able to do that.
anchors.note: A specific, dated and substantial cash event roughly three weeks out, tied to materials arriving from Spain. The rep correctly diarised against it, but never proposed the obvious structure — a small payment now to start immediately with the balance on the cheque — which would have preserved the momentum the prospect explicitly said he did not want to lose.

anchors.raw: We do financing at roofing, right? And so most of them are like a soft credit pool and you put in your income and all the stats and they give you accepted for X amount of dollars.
anchors.note: Sells consumer financing for a living and was entirely comfortable running a soft check on the call. Unusual in this corpus, where financing has generally been introduced by the rep against buyer resistance. Notable that despite this comfort no monthly figure was ever quoted to him, so he could not evaluate the option he was most equipped to evaluate.

unmet_demand.want: A price or structure his household can carry now, asked for directly — 'tell me what were the lowest that y'all would comfortably accept'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is a single price and no sanctioned lower tier for this rep to offer. He held the line correctly, but the prospect left with no monthly figure for the financing option either, so he goes into a budget conversation with his wife armed only with '$6,000' and 'there is financing'. A quoted monthly number would have cost nothing and is the one thing that conversation needs.

unmet_demand.want: To train alongside his wife — 'she'll probably be doing this with me as well, right? So it's going to benefit both of us'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No couple, partner or family offering exists, and the rep did not engage with it. This matters commercially here more than usual: the person who controls the budget is also a prospective participant, and framing the spend as covering a shared activity would have changed the household calculation rather than just the timing.

unmet_demand.want: Resolution of the recurring right knee problem so he can hike in the Arkansas mountains with his sons
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no clinical layer, and the rep answered with an assertion instead — that 95% of the time it is simply a strengthening issue, plus a dismissal of ankle-support footwear. The prospect himself said 'I don't think it's a tendon thing, I don't know what's going on.' Whether the programme fixes it, ignores it or aggravates it is unestablished, and it is one of his stated reasons for buying.

unmet_demand.want: Reassurance about training hard with a possible hereditary cardiac condition in the family
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised it as part of why he needs this — an uncle and that uncle's father both dead of heart attacks — and received no response whatsoever. The offer contains no cardiac screening, no clearance step and no clinician, and the disclosure did not even prompt an acknowledgement. He is buying partly as heart-disease prevention from a product that makes no claim on it either way.
